PATIENT JOURNEY — Sprint 1 wireframes

Symptom check → urgency suggestion → slot → confirmation.
The assistant never diagnoses, and a red flag stops the conversation and routes to 999.

Built so far: dashboard, sign-in, registration. The rest is Sprint 2–3.
The conflict state is the one that matters. Two patients can want 10:20 at the same instant, so the database — not the UI — decides who gets it. The loser is told plainly that nothing was booked.

CLINICAL — access is earned, not assumed

A clinician sees records they are assigned to. Anything else needs emergency access with a typed reason, which expires and is logged.

Priority flags are a suggestion from a symptom checker. They are never presented as a decision.

The approval gate.

An AI draft is not the record. It becomes the record only when a named clinician approves it, and the original draft is kept unchanged alongside their edits.

There is no default, and no timeout that approves on its own.

OPERATIONS — aggregates, never identities

Administrators see that a record was accessed, not whose. Operational authority is not clinical authority.

Model monitoring shows behaviour. It is not clinical governance and does not replace a safety case.
Shared patterns every screen inherits, so the six states and the accessibility rules are decided once rather than per page.
